findings.issue: Future aggregate verification never verifies raw receipt bytes or their semantic content.
findings.evidence: assertNativeReceipts checks only that there are four entries, each has a nonempty path and each hash is syntactically SHA-256. It never opens or hashes those paths, checks required receipt names, or revalidates run identity/legs/provider outcomes. An isolated call to the exact extracted candidate function accepted four references to a confirmed nonexistent file with all-zero digests.
findings.fix: Preserve raw receipt evidence in an immutable form available to subsequent verification, such as bytes embedded in the allowed proof artifact or a durable content-addressed artifact. Require exactly manifest, teardown, provider_correlation and selector_log; read the retained bytes and verify their hashes, then validate original run IDs/timestamps, complete native legs and required provider outcomes. Reject missing or changed bytes. Do not rely on mutable .tmp paths that later selectors overwrite. Add discriminating negative checks using the actual verifier and real receipt files.

findings.issue: Proof completeness is accepted from counts without checking selector identities, executed-test counts or native leg identities.
findings.evidence: assertRecordedSelectors accepts six copies of {name:docs-collection,exit:0} while native_proof.selector_count is 2; the native receipt loop then executes zero times. assertSelectorGreen accepts exit 0 with output Tests 4 skipped (4), because tallyOf is never enforced. passedLegCount accepts five duplicated passed iOS legs without requiring Android or Web.
findings.fix: Require the exact six unique selector names and commands, exact expected passed-test counts (4,4,1,1,1,1) and zero failed tests in fresh and recorded proof. Derive the native selector count from the actual named records and require both marathon records. Validate the exact native platform/appearance set, including Web, with no duplicates or missing targets. Add negative checks for missing/duplicate selectors, all-skipped output and duplicate platform legs.

findings.issue: Ordinary aggregate verification requires historical Git objects unavailable in the existing shallow hosted checkout.
findings.evidence: verifyRecordedGreen calls assertRecordedScope, which calls candidateScope and cat-file for TASK_BASE_COMMIT plus the historical execution candidate. It then calls assertGitAndCurrentHashes, which git-shows each file at that historical candidate. The parent independently verified the current CI checkout is default depth 1 with detached HEAD and missing historical objects. No local main dependency exists here, but the historical-object dependency is enough to fail ordinary hosted aggregate verification. The separately collected aggregate-owner-routing.test.ts also unconditionally diffs 8ee4282f..f9d30b09, so its ordinary aggregate path has the same shallow-history failure.
findings.fix: Keep the real Git range and candidate-byte audit at execution/review time. Ordinary aggregate verification must validate the immutable recorded boundary, exact selector/raw-receipt evidence and current executable/input hashes from the durable proof artifact without requiring historical Git objects. Add an isolated real shallow-clone check that passes a valid bound artifact and rejects changed current bytes or altered evidence, without native execution. Apply the same execution-audit versus durable-verification separation to the routing test; never silently skip a missing historical audit.
